editorial.marketOverview: Thursday's US close remains the anchor: Nasdaq -2.25%, S&P -2.02%, broad decliners and VIX 28.44. Overnight Asian technology shares continued to slide; AP reported Nikkei and Kospi approximately -4.5%, and FT reported TSMC -4.5%. The overnight futures indication was negative, but Friday US cash trading has not begun.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to 21:53 EST, AP and FT supply additional evidence of Asian semiconductor selling, while IBD reports Nasdaq-100 futures down approximately 0.5% overnight. This is further corroboration of existing risk aversion, not a newly established US-market directional break. The Open Watch file has no fresh timestamp since the prior review.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Global semiconductor selling increases the risk that Friday US QQQ and SOX open weak. The inference remains conditional: regional trading, overnight futures and US closing breadth are asynchronous. AP's indicative 10-year yield of 5.04% does not provide a synchronized 2-year curve, and declining yields can reflect defensive positioning rather than improved equity appetite.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20 is the first test: watch whether QQQ and SOX stabilize against SPY after the open and how equities respond to 10:00 EST Michigan sentiment. Continued weak breadth and failed bounces would favor downside continuation Monday November 23 and Tuesday November 24. A durable semiconductor-led rebound would invalidate that scenario.
editorial.bullCase: An oversold bounce is plausible after sustained selling; it requires actual Friday QQQ/SPY outperformance, SOX/SMH strength, improving participation and falling VXN/VIX, rather than an isolated IPO premium or a lower Treasury yield.
editorial.bearCase: The broad Thursday US selloff and Asian Friday semiconductor losses support a bearish baseline. A weak US Friday open followed by failure to recover and broad downside volume would favor further losses into Monday; this remains a scenario, not a verified Friday market reaction.
